title: The history of the aeroplane
tagline: From Cayley's sketches and Lilienthal's gliders to the Wright brothers, Indian pilots and the jets of today.
intro: People knew that a curved wing could carry a load long before anyone flew in a powered machine. Gliders taught wing design, but the Wright brothers' steering and engine made flight practical in 1903. In India, Tata's licence and the Indian Air Force followed in the 1930s.

eras.name: The idea
eras.summary: Engineers worked out the parts: a curved wing, a separate push and a steering tail. Gliders taught people how a wing carries a load, and the Wright brothers added control.

eras.name: First flights
eras.summary: Powered flight went from a 12-second hop to crossings of the sea. Each record was a test of the aeroplane's control and endurance.

eras.name: India takes off
eras.summary: The first airmail in India flew in 1911. Indian pilots, the Indian Air Force and Indian aircraft makers followed, starting in the 1930s.

eras.name: Jets and the sky today
eras.summary: Jet engines replaced the propeller on big aircraft. Turbofans, wide-body airliners and modern regional flights carry most of the world's passengers today.

events.title: Cayley sets out the parts of an aeroplane
events.text: Cayley argued that lift, thrust and control should be separate jobs: a fixed curved wing, a separate push, and a movable tail. Most histories date this idea to 1799.
events.why: It is the blueprint that every later aeroplane followed.

events.title: Cayley's glider carries a person
events.text: Accounts say his glider carried a coachman a short distance down a hill. The details differ between sources, so treat this flight as less certain.
events.why: It showed that a fixed wing could carry a person through the air.

events.title: Ader's Éole takes off under its own power
events.text: The Éole rose from level ground under its own power and covered about 50 metres, a few tens of centimetres high. It could not be steered well, and Ader's later claims are disputed.
events.why: It was an early powered take-off, though control was not solved.

events.title: Lilienthal's gliders
events.text: Between 1891 and 1896 Otto Lilienthal made thousands of glides in hang gliders of his own design. He steered by shifting his body under the wing.
events.why: His careful data and flights taught the next generation how wings carry loads.

events.title: The Wright brothers fly
events.where: Kill Devil Hills, North Carolina, USA
events.text: Orville flew about 120 feet (36.6 m) in 12 seconds. On the fourth flight, Wilbur flew 852 feet in 59 seconds. The brothers had also built a way to steer in the air.
events.why: It was the first controlled, powered, sustained flight of a heavier-than-air machine.

events.title: Santos-Dumont flies the 14-bis in Paris
events.text: The 14-bis made a powered hop in front of a crowd and in front of cameras. Some records give other dates for later flights.
events.why: It was one of the first powered flights witnessed and filmed in public.

events.title: Blériot crosses the Channel
events.text: Blériot flew a single-seat monoplane from near Calais to Dover in about 36 to 37 minutes. Sources differ slightly on the time.
events.why: It was a public sensation and showed that an aeroplane could cross the sea.

events.title: The first airmail flight in India
events.text: Pequet flew a biplane about 10 km from a polo field to Naini, carrying about 6,500 letters and cards marked for the exhibition in Allahabad.
events.why: It is often recorded as the first official airmail flight in the world.

events.title: Alcock and Brown fly the Atlantic non-stop
events.who: John Alcock and Arthur Whitten Brown
events.where: St John's, Newfoundland to Clifden, Ireland
events.text: In a twin-engined Vickers Vimy they flew about 3,000 km overnight, through fog and snow. They landed in a bog they had mistaken for a field.
events.why: It was the first non-stop crossing of the Atlantic by air.

events.title: Lindbergh flies New York to Paris alone
events.text: Lindbergh flew solo in the Spirit of St. Louis for 33.5 hours, covering about 5,800 km.
events.why: It won the $25,000 Orteig Prize and drew public attention to long-distance flight.

events.title: J.R.D. Tata becomes India's first licensed pilot
events.text: Tata received licence No. 1 issued in India. Sources differ on the licence class.
events.why: Indian aviation began with Indian pilots holding Indian licences.

events.title: Tata's airmail flight from Karachi to Bombay
events.text: Tata flew a single-engine de Havilland Puss Moth from Karachi to Juhu, stopping at Ahmedabad, with about 25 kg of letters.
events.why: It was the start of Tata's airline, later Air India.

events.date: 8 October 1932 (Gazette date; the Act passed earlier in 1932)
events.title: The Indian Air Force is set up
events.text: The Indian Air Force was created as an auxiliary of the Royal Air Force. A Bharat-Rakshak article notes that the Act was passed in April 1932 and that 8 October is the Gazette date.
events.why: It began India's own air arm, which later became the Royal Indian Air Force and then the Indian Air Force.

events.title: First squadron of the Indian Air Force
events.text: No. 1 Squadron was commissioned with four Westland Wapiti biplanes and five Indian pilots.
events.why: It turned the new air force into a working unit.

events.title: Whittle's first jet engine run
events.text: Whittle's first test run went badly: the engine sped up out of control. Historians still count it as the first run of a turbojet, though it was not built to fly.
events.why: It was the first test of the jet engine idea that changed flight.

events.title: The first jet-powered flight
events.text: The Heinkel He 178 flew on the thrust of a turbojet on 27 August 1939. The flight lasted about six minutes.
events.why: It showed that a jet engine could power a flying aircraft.

events.title: The de Havilland Comet first flies
events.who: de Havilland; test pilot John Cunningham
events.text: The Comet, the first commercial jet airliner, made its maiden flight from Hatfield. BOAC began the first jet passenger service in May 1952.
events.why: It started the jet age for passengers and cut long-distance travel times.

events.title: The first jet airliner enters passenger service
events.text: BOAC began the first scheduled jet passenger service with the Comet on 2 May 1952.
events.why: Jets began carrying fare-paying passengers.

events.title: The HF-24 Marut flies
events.text: HAL's HF-24 Marut, designed in India, made its first flight on 17 June 1961. A pre-production test aircraft had flown earlier, in 1959.
events.why: It was an early Indian-designed jet fighter.

events.title: The Boeing 747 first flies
events.text: The 747 first flew on 9 February 1969 and was certified in December 1969. It is a wide-body airliner with two aisles.
events.why: It carried far more passengers than earlier jets and made long-haul flying cheaper per seat.

events.title: Tejas, India's light combat aircraft, first flies
events.text: The first technology demonstrator, TD-1 of the Light Combat Aircraft programme, flew on 4 January 2001.
events.why: It was the start of India's own light combat aircraft.

events.title: UDAN launches to connect smaller cities
events.text: The Regional Connectivity Scheme, UDAN ('Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik'), launched on 21 October 2016. Airlines bid for routes, and the government funds part of the gap in costs for flights to smaller airports.
events.why: It was India's main scheme to bring affordable flights to smaller cities.

people.name: Sir George Cayley
people.note: Separated lift, thrust and control, and built gliders that carried a person.

people.name: Otto Lilienthal
people.note: Made thousands of glides and steered by moving his body under the wing.

people.name: Henri Pequet
people.note: Flew the first Indian airmail at Allahabad in 1911.

people.name: J.R.D. Tata
people.note: Held India's first licence and flew the first Indian airmail in 1932.

people.name: Frank Whittle
people.note: Designed the first practical jet engine and ran it in 1937.

series.title: The longest single flight, by distance
series.caption: Each point is a single flight. The Wright brothers' first flight covered 36.6 metres.

facts: The Wright brothers' first flight lasted 12 seconds. Their fourth flight the same day lasted 59.
Pequet's 1911 mail flight at Allahabad carried about 6,500 letters.
Lindbergh's solo flight across the Atlantic took 33.5 hours.
The first Indian licence, No. 1, was issued to J.R.D. Tata in February 1929.
ICAO's 2024 figure is about 2.6 accidents per million departures for scheduled commercial flights.
